title: Mentzer Heavy Duty II Ideal Program
author: Silver P.
desc: Unlock your strength potential with the Mentzer Heavy Duty II Ideal Routine, a focused program designed for serious lifters looking to maximize muscle growth in minimal time. This split routine emphasizes high-intensity training, allowing for optimal recovery while targeting major muscle groups effectively. Commit to high intensity workouts that blend compound lifts with isolation exercises, ensuring you build strength and size efficiently. Perfect for those ready to push their limits and see results fast!

ss.note: If unavailable, sub flat bench DB flyes or cable crossovers. No dedicated warm-up needed here — see next exercise.

Superset immediately after Pec Deck. Fairly close grip (hands slightly closer than shoulder width); flare elbows back toward ears — NOT a wide grip. If no machine, use free-weight barbell or DB incline press. Per Mentzer: whenever two exercises are supersetted, do your warm-up sets on the SECOND exercise before starting the superset — that way you're warmed up for both and the weight is already set. · Warm-up: 1–2 light sets, ~15–20 reps, on THIS exercise before the superset
No superset — rest as long as needed, but don't dawdle. · Warm-up: 1–2 light sets, ~15–20 reps, well short of failure

ex.note: Most productive exercise in the program — warm up carefully given the loading and technical demand. Bar rolled back against shins; grip slightly wider than shoulder width, interlocking (one hand over, one under); hips slightly lower than shoulders; back perfectly flat, head up (pick a spot on the wall and hold your eyes there). Stand up fully with hip rotation — no backward arch. If lower back is an issue, substitute Shrugs for 6–10 reps. · Warm-up: 1–2 light sets working up to your top weight (e.g., bar/45s, then a mid-weight single or double)

ss.note: Superset with Leg Press. Warm-up sets are done on the 2nd exercise of the superset (leg press) — see next row.

If no leg press, sub Squats (preferably Smith machine). No leg curls in this phase — hamstrings get enough work from deadlift/leg press/squat. Per Mentzer: warm up on the 2nd exercise of a superset so both movements — and the leg extension weight — are ready to go. · Warm-up: 1–2 light sets, ~15–20 reps, on THIS exercise before the superset

ex.note: Rest a couple minutes after the leg superset (walk around, get water) before this. · Warm-up: 1–2 light sets, ~15–20 reps, well short of failure
